compiled_state.title: As an engineer, the grep handler enforces wall-clock timeout and binary-file exclusion to prevent ReDoS
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Add the `grep` handler with wall-clock timeout (default 5s) and binary-file exclusion (or use ripgrep with `--max-filesize`). Same realpath-canonicalized jail as read_files.

**Why**: SC2 grep portion. Without timeout, an adversarial regex like `(a+)+$` against a long line can pin a CI core indefinitely; without binary exclusion, the handler returns garbled output that wastes context.

**Scope**:
- IN: grep handler with multi-pattern multi-path argument shape; per-invocation wall-clock timeout (configurable, default 5s); binary-file exclusion (or ripgrep `--max-filesize`); per-result max output bytes (default 64 KB) with truncation marker
- OUT: changes to read_files handler; changes to parser; integration with multi-turn loop (covered by S5)

## Done Definitions

- When complete, an adversarial regex (e.g., `(a+)+$`) against a long line aborts at the wall-clock timeout and returns a clear timeout error rather than hanging ← Satisfies: SC2 (grep ReDoS defense)
- When complete, grep on a directory containing binary files skips them silently (or via documented exclusion) without including binary content in the result ← Satisfies: SC2 (binary exclusion)
- When complete, unit tests written and passing for timeout enforcement, binary exclusion, multi-pattern multi-path argument acceptance, and output-bytes truncation ← Satisfies: SC6 (unit tests for grep portion)

## Considerations

- [Security] Timeout is a denial-of-service mitigation; default 5s is conservative — may need tuning per CI runner perf
- [Reliability] Prefer ripgrep when available for built-in size/binary handling

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
